cues.en: This
cues.zh: This

cues.en: is John Coltrane's Giant Steps.
cues.zh: 这是John Coltrane的《Giant Steps》。

cues.en: It's considered one of the most important jazz albums of all time. It cemented John Coltrane as a legend among jazz saxophonists and composers,
cues.zh: 它被认为是有史以来最重要的爵士专辑之一。它奠定了John Coltrane作为爵士萨克斯手和作曲家传奇人物的地位，

cues.en: and it's home to one of the most revered and feared compositions
cues.zh: 其中还收录了爵士史上最受崇敬也最令人望而生畏的作曲之一

cues.en: in jazz history.
The reason why the album's title track is so iconic
cues.zh: 这张专辑的同名曲之所以如此标志性

cues.en: can be heard in its first few seconds.
cues.zh: 从它的前几秒就能听出来。

cues.en: Coltrane wrote these unique chord changes changes for Giant Steps and later went on to use them over traditional jazz standards.
cues.zh: Coltrane为《Giant Steps》写下了这些独特的和弦进行，后来又把它们用在传统爵士标准曲上。

cues.en: These chords came to be known as the Coltrane changes and improvising over them is considered a rite of passage for jazz musicians.
cues.zh: 这些和弦后来被称为Coltrane changes，在其上即兴演奏被视为爵士音乐人的一道成人礼。

cues.en: But if you don't understand a lick of music theory like me, it's really hard to see how this
cues.zh: 但如果你像我一样对乐理一窍不通，就很难看出这

cues.en: is so legendary.
cues.zh: 到底为什么如此传奇。

cues.en: Lucky for me, I know two people that could explain why.
cues.zh: 幸运的是，我认识两个能解释原因的人。

cues.en: Braxton Cook. Okay.
cues.zh: Braxton Cook。好的。

cues.en: I did the... Okay. You caught me. I'm guard and Adam Neely. Should I get into the, like, technical jargony stuff? Let's cut to the logo first.
cues.zh: 我做了……好吧，被你发现了。我是Guard，还有Adam Neely。我该不该讲那些技术黑话？先切到片头logo吧。

cues.en: So there's a moment in the Giant Steps recording that really illustrates just how demanding this song is.
cues.zh: 《Giant Steps》的录音里有一个瞬间，真正体现了这首歌有多难。

cues.en: It happens when Tommy Flanagan,
cues.zh: 那发生在Tommy Flanagan——

cues.en: the pianist on the record, starts his solo.
cues.zh: 唱片里的钢琴手——开始他的独奏时。

cues.en: The story goes, John Coltrane brought in the music. You know, he shows up ready to go and then he calls this really fast tempo,
cues.zh: 据说John Coltrane带来了乐谱。你知道，他准备好就来了，然后他定了一个非常快的速度，

cues.en: you know.
cues.zh: 你知道的。

cues.en: If you hear on the recording, Tommy Flanagan
cues.zh: 如果你听录音，Tommy Flanagan

cues.en: just cannot handle
cues.zh: 根本跟不上

cues.en: the chord progressions as they're going by. His improvisation is very halted.
cues.zh: 那些和弦进行的速度。他的即兴非常断续。

cues.en: And Tommy Flanagan is holding on for dear life. It really becomes apparent how much he struggled when you hear Coltrane take off at lightning speed the second Flanagan stops.
cues.zh: Tommy Flanagan 在拼命硬撑。当 Flanagan 一停下来，Coltrane 就以闪电般的速度起飞，这时候你就能明显听出他有多吃力。

cues.en: And then it goes down as like one of the most legendary recordings of all time. That's messed up. I would want another shot, know. I'd be like, bro, don't put that recording up. To understand why this is so difficult for even a highly trained pianist, we need to know three basic concepts.
cues.zh: 然后这段录音就成了史上最传奇的录音之一。这太坑了。我会想再来一次，你懂吧。我会说，兄弟，别把那段录音放出来。要理解为什么这对即使训练有素的钢琴家来说都如此困难，我们需要了解三个基本概念。

cues.en: And it all starts with this,
cues.zh: 一切都要从这个东西说起，

cues.en: the circle of fifths.
cues.zh: 五度圈。

cues.en: It's kind of like a color wheel for music. Okay. Awesome. You glued this stuff and everything. This is fire. All 12 notes of the western musical scale are on it, but you might notice they're a little mixed up.
cues.zh: 它有点像音乐里的色轮。好。太棒了。你把这些东西都粘起来了。这太酷了。西方音阶的全部12个音都在上面，但你可能会注意到它们有点打乱了顺序。

cues.en: That's because they're organized by a very special number in music,
cues.zh: 那是因为它们是按照音乐中一个非常特殊的数字来组织的，

cues.en: a fifth.
cues.zh: 一个五度。

cues.en: What's a fifth? It's like if we were in the c major scale, we go c d e f g. Right? One two three four five.
cues.zh: 什么是五度？就像如果我们在C大调音阶里，我们走C D E F G。对吧？一 二 三 四 五。

cues.en: From c to g is five notes, from g to d is five notes, and well, you get the idea.
cues.zh: 从C到G是五个音，从G到D是五个音，嗯，你懂这个意思了。

cues.en: If you play through circle, you'll traverse the entire keyboard starting on the lowest c
cues.zh: 如果你沿着这个圈弹下去，你会遍历整个键盘，从最低的C开始

cues.en: and ending up on the highest c.
cues.zh: 最后到最高的C。

cues.en: It sounds much more harmonious
cues.zh: 听起来和谐得多

cues.en: than just playing all the notes in order.
cues.zh: 比只是按顺序弹所有的音要好听得多。

cues.en: That's because... The fifth is a sound that our ears just like.
cues.zh: 那是因为……五度是我们耳朵就是喜欢的声音。

cues.en: Please explain. Whenever we're hearing anything, whenever we're hearing people sing, whenever we're hearing people play music, we're hearing these other notes, these overtones alongside
cues.zh: 请解释一下。每当我们听到任何声音，每当我们听到人们唱歌，每当我们听到人们演奏音乐，我们都在听到这些其他的音，这些泛音，伴随着

cues.en: the pitches that they're playing. When I play this c, the first two loudest tones that are pushed through the air are both c.
cues.zh: 他们正在演奏的音高。当我弹这个C时，被推入空气中的前两个最响的音都是C。

cues.en: One is just an octave higher.
cues.zh: 其中一个只是高了八度。

cues.en: But other tones travel to our ears as well. The third loudest is a g which happens to be a fifth above c.
cues.zh: 但其他音也会传入我们的耳朵。响度排第三的是 G 音，正好比 C 音高一个五度。

cues.en: In 1973, Leonard Bernstein demonstrated this phenomenon
cues.zh: 1973 年，Leonard Bernstein 演示了这一现象，

cues.en: live on a grand piano at Harvard.
cues.zh: 当时是在哈佛大学的一台三角钢琴上现场展示的。

cues.en: Listen closely after he hits that note.
cues.zh: 仔细听他弹下那个音之后的声音。

cues.en: What do we hear now?
cues.zh: 我们现在听到了什么？

cues.en: That g. Right? A new tone. Again, clear as a bell. You wanna hear it again?
cues.zh: 那个 G 音，对吧？一个全新的音。依然清晰无比。想再听一遍吗？

cues.en: These overtones are kind of like subliminal tones that you're hearing alongside
cues.zh: 这些泛音有点像潜意识中的声音，它们伴随着

cues.en: a regular note and you're hearing these overtones
cues.zh: 一个普通的音符出现，而且你随时随地

cues.en: everywhere.
cues.zh: 都能听到这种泛音。

cues.en: A lot of western music is based on the power of the fifth,
cues.zh: 很多西方音乐都建立在五度音的力量之上，

cues.en: especially how it relates so strongly back to its home chord. In the case of the key of c major, we have the g chord resolving to c.
cues.zh: 尤其是它与主和弦之间极其强烈的呼应关系。以 C 大调为例，就是 G 和弦解决到 C 和弦。

cues.en: If we're thinking about what the g chord represents, it represents kind of tension.
cues.zh: 如果思考 G 和弦代表什么，它代表着一种张力。

cues.en: You want this to resolve.
cues.zh: 你会迫切希望这种张力得到解决。

cues.en: And when it finally does resolve,
cues.zh: 而当它最终解决时，

cues.en: it creates this feeling of finality. It creates a feeling of home.
cues.zh: 便营造出一种尘埃落定的感觉，一种归宿感。

cues.en: That five to one relationship is present in a lot of chord progressions,
cues.zh: 这种五级到一级的关系存在于很多和弦进行中，

cues.en: including the most common one found in jazz,
cues.zh: 包括爵士乐中最常见的一种——

cues.en: the two five one. The two five one essentially is like the backbone of most jazz music. Even in its most basic form, it sounds super jazzy.
cues.zh: 二五一进行。二五一基本上就是绝大多数爵士乐的脊梁骨。哪怕是最基础的形式，听起来也极具爵士味。

cues.en: And this is the
cues.zh: 这可以说是

cues.en: kind of the building blocks of most of jazz. So it comes as no surprise the Coltrane changes are just chock full of them, which might raise the question.
cues.zh: 大部分爵士乐的基石。所以 Coltrane changes 里充斥着这种进行也就不足为奇了，但这可能会引出一个问题。

cues.en: Why was Tommy Flanagan caught off guard when he had to improvise over them?
cues.zh: 为什么Tommy Flanagan即兴演奏这些和声时会措手不及？

cues.en: Well, the Coltrane changes aren't in one key.
cues.zh: 因为Coltrane变化不在一个调上。

cues.en: They're in three keys.
cues.zh: 它们涉及三个调。

cues.en: They're basically a musical M. C. Escher painting.
cues.zh: 基本上就像一幅音乐版的M. C. Escher画作。

cues.en: So each one of these rungs on the circle of fifths represents every possible key center.
cues.zh: 五度圈上的每一格代表一个可能的调中心。

cues.en: The closer a key is to another, the more notes they have in common.
cues.zh: 两个调越接近，共有的音符就越多。

cues.en: Like the c major and g major scale, they're only different by one note, an f sharp.
cues.zh: 比如C大调和G大调音阶，只差一个音，升F。

cues.en: Okay. We need an analogy to describe this. So the way that I like to think about keys is kind of like languages that you have to learn as a jazz improviser. You have to be able to be fluent in a key. Like maybe c is Spanish and g is Portuguese.
cues.zh: 好，我们需要一个类比来描述这个。我倾向于把调想象成爵士即兴者必须学习的语言。你得能流利掌握一个调。比如C可能像西班牙语，G像葡萄牙语。

cues.en: Those are very similar languages.
cues.zh: 这两种语言非常相似。

cues.en: That's the case, like, okay, maybe c is Spanish and you have a distantly related language like maybe Japanese.
cues.zh: 那如果情况是这样呢，C是西班牙语，而另一种是关系较远的语言，比如日语。

cues.en: Let's say Japanese is b. There's not much in common with those two languages and it's the same with keys. If you play those scales over each other,
cues.zh: 假设日语对应B。这两种语言没什么共同点，调也是一样。如果你把这些音阶叠在一起弹，

cues.en: it sounds a lot more discordant.
cues.zh: 听起来会不和谐得多。

cues.en: For the most part, most pop music is based around one of these key centers. For instance, Carly Rae Jepsen's Cut to the Feeling is in a major.
cues.zh: 大部分流行音乐都围绕其中一个调中心。比如Carly Rae Jepsen的Cut to the Feeling是A大调。

cues.en: But some songs modulate to another key for dramatic effect,
cues.zh: 但有些歌会转到另一个调来制造戏剧效果，

cues.en: like Beyonce's Love On Top. Everything stops
cues.zh: 比如Beyonce的Love On Top。一切都停下来

cues.en: finally.
cues.zh: 终于。

cues.en: Put my love on top. Baby,
cues.zh: 把我的爱放在顶端。宝贝，

cues.en: you're the one that I love.
cues.zh: 你是我所爱的人。

cues.en: Part of the reason why it's really exciting is because you're going to a place that's really distant on the circle of fifths. And you're creating a new sense of home, which is exactly what Love on Top does.
cues.zh: 它之所以令人兴奋，部分原因在于你会去到五度圈上非常遥远的地方。同时你又在创造一种新的归属感，这正是 Love on Top 所做的。

cues.en: But it doesn't just happen once, it happens every time she repeats the chorus towards the end of the song.
cues.zh: 但这不只发生一次；她在歌曲结尾附近每次重复副歌时都会发生。

cues.en: And when we chart that sort thing along the circle of fifths, patterns emerge.
cues.zh: 当我们把这类东西标在五度圈上时，规律就会显现出来。

cues.en: These types of patterns are what fascinated John Coltrane in the late nineteen fifties and sixties
cues.zh: 这类模式正是 John Coltrane 在二十世纪五十年代末和六十年代着迷的东西。

cues.en: as he was trying to push jazz harmony to its limits.
cues.zh: 当时他正试图把爵士和声推向极限。

cues.en: This is his study of the circle of fifths. I think what makes Giant Steps really special is that it really just it just documented
cues.zh: 这是他对五度圈的研究。我觉得 Giant Steps 真正特别的地方在于，它真的只是……它只是记录下了

cues.en: an artist doing something super
cues.zh: 一位艺术家在做某种极其

cues.en: unique, super stylistic,
cues.zh: 独特、极具风格，

cues.en: and virtuosic at the same time.
cues.zh: 同时又炫技。

cues.en: Here's the first 16 bars of giant steps again with just the key changes highlighted.
cues.zh: 这里再次是 Giant Steps 的前 16 小节，只突出显示调性变化。

cues.en: If you chart those changes on the circle of fifths, it comes out as a pretty dramatic pattern.
cues.zh: 如果你把这些变化标在五度圈上，会呈现出一个相当引人注目的图形。

cues.en: That's because these keys are separated
cues.zh: 这是因为这些调之间相隔

cues.en: by major thirds,
cues.zh: 大三度，

cues.en: which divide an octave into three equal parts. On the circle of fifths, these three keys are as far apart as possible from each other. Giant Steps is kind of like you're shifting from Spanish to Arabic to Japanese very quickly. By quickly, he means like every two beats in a song that's nearly 300 beats per minute. It's not only just like you're saying one word per language,
cues.zh: 它们把八度分成三等份。在五度圈上，这三个调彼此之间尽可能远。Giant Steps 有点像你非常快地从西班牙语切换到阿拉伯语，再切换到日语。所谓快，他指的是在接近每分钟 300 拍的歌里，大约每两拍就切换一次。这不仅像是你每种语言只说一个词，

cues.en: you're having to construct a sentence out of the language.
cues.zh: 你还得用这种语言构造出一个句子。

cues.en: And how does Coltrane make those disparate languages connect?
cues.zh: 那么 Coltrane 是如何将这些截然不同的语言串联起来的呢？

cues.en: With one of the most ubiquitous phrases in jazz,
cues.zh: 靠的是爵士乐中最常见的一个乐句，

cues.en: the five one.
cues.zh: 也就是“五一进行”。

cues.en: What he's doing is taking some of the conventional ideas of tonal harmony, conventional relationships between the five chord and the one chord, and applying it to this very chaotic
cues.zh: 他所做的，是借鉴调式和声的传统概念，即五级和弦与一级和弦之间的经典关系，并将其应用到这种极度混乱的、

cues.en: circling sort of chord progression that is the Coltrane changes.
cues.zh: 循环往复的和弦进行中——也就是 Coltrane changes。

cues.en: So if we were all in the same key, it would sound like this.
cues.zh: 如果全都在同一个调上，听起来会是这样。

cues.en: But because we're going from key center to key center, it sounds very different.
cues.zh: 但因为我们在不同的调性中心之间不断切换，听起来就完全不同了。

cues.en: This
cues.zh: 这

cues.en: is why the Coltrane changes are like this picture here. Even though you're seeing things from a completely new perspective and place, you still feel like you've made it home somehow.
cues.zh: 就是为什么 Coltrane changes 就像这里的这幅图一样。即便你从一个全新的视角和位置看去，却依然会觉得以某种方式回到了原点。

cues.en: When Tommy Flanagan saw the charts for Giant Steps, he knew he wasn't going to just have to play this chord progression, he was going to have to improvise over it very quickly. That was probably so funny. He was probably like, what? It is a bit of a rite of passage to say that you not only can improvise in Giant Steps,
cues.zh: 当 Tommy Flanagan 看到《Giant Steps》的和弦谱时，他知道自己不仅要弹下这套和弦进行，还得在极快的速度下进行即兴。当时一定很有意思，他大概心想“什么鬼？”。能说出自己不仅能在《Giant Steps》上即兴，

cues.en: but you can also improvise in all 12 keys.
cues.zh: 而且能在全部 12 个调里即兴，本身就像是一种成年礼。

cues.en: Now generations of jazz musicians are approaching Giant Steps as the sort of pinnacle of improvisation.
cues.zh: 如今，一代代爵士乐手都把《Giant Steps》视作即兴演奏的某种巅峰。

cues.en: Wait. I think I've got an analogy for this.
cues.zh: 等等，我想到了一个比喻。

cues.en: It's like you're a cab driver and instead of knowing only one way to get somewhere, you have to know every back alley and side street just in case. It's essentially like that. You still get to the same location but it's really interesting and you might see some really cool stuff in the neighborhood. But ultimately, I still think the music like boils down to five one.
cues.zh: 就像你是个出租车司机，为了以防万一，你不能只知道一条路线，而是得熟悉每条后巷和小街。本质上就是这样，你最终还是能到达同一个目的地，但过程非常有趣，沿途还能看到周围很酷的风景。不过归根结底，我觉得音乐的核心依然是那个“五一进行”。

cues.en: People wanna come back home.
cues.zh: 人们想回到家乡。

cues.en: Thanks so much for watching the first of three videos I'm gonna release in the next couple of weeks on jazz.
cues.zh: 非常感谢你观看接下来几周我会发布的三个爵士乐视频中的第一个。

cues.en: I wanna give a special thanks to Braxton Cook and Adam Neely. Between the time that I interviewed Braxton and now he's released a full album, please check it out below and of course special special thanks to Adam Neely. You can check out his YouTube channel below. Until next time.
cues.zh: 我要特别感谢 Braxton Cook 和 Adam Neely。从我采访 Braxton 到现在这段时间里，他已经发布了一张完整专辑，请在下方查看；当然还要特别特别感谢 Adam Neely。你可以在下方查看他的 YouTube 频道。下次见。
